Background

The Green Climate Fund is the world’s largest dedicated multilateral climate fund and invests in impactful, innovative, catalytic programs and projects in developing countries across the globe As we celebrate 10 years of climate action, our portfolio has grown to over USD 22.3 billion across more than 379 projects in over 134 countries — demonstrating the transformative power of strategic climate finance at scale. In 2023, an additional USD 12.8 billion was pledged, to support our new strategic and programming cycle from 2024-2027; our ambition is to grow to become at least a USD 50 billion fund by 2030. Rooted in the core objectives of impact and efficiency, access and a focus on the most vulnerable, and mobilizing unprecedented public and private sector financial flows for climate action we have unparalleled scale and resources. Our risk appetite and flexibility enable us to bring together diverse partners and stakeholders in innovative partnerships for profound impact.

The Fund seeks to recruit a Senior Fiduciary Consultant (“Fiduciary Expert”) to assist the Accreditation Panel (“AP”) of GCF in carrying out the tasks, duties and responsibilities set out below, delivering the agreed outputs, and providing support to the hiring unit as required. The consultant will work remotely.

The assignment is for an initial 120 working days over a 12-month period, with an expected input of up to 15 working days per month, subject to workload and with flexibility in the distribution of days.
Role

The Fiduciary Expert will assist the Secretariat and the AP in the operationalization of the revised Accreditation Framework (“RAF”). The work will focus on assessing accreditation applications against the applicable fiduciary screening requirements, applying a fit-for-purpose approach, and supporting the development of relevant guidance for the accreditation process as needed.
Duties and responsibilities
The Consultant will be responsible for, but not limited to, the following:
(a) Support and/or conduct the assessment of accreditation applications as they relate to the Fund’s fiduciary standards, to the extent applicable to accreditation;

(b) Apply sound technical judgement in reviewing institutional systems, policies, procedures and evidence of implementation against the applicable fiduciary screening requirements, including where evidence is mixed or differs from expected international practice;

(c) Identify material gaps, formulate focused requests for additional information, assess applicant responses, and contribute to clear, evidence-based findings and recommendations for consideration by the AP;

(d) Attend meetings by video conference, as required, and provide comments in meetings with the applicants, the Secretariat, Accreditation Committee, Accreditation Panel and, where relevant, Board members during the accreditation process;

(e) Attend Board meetings by video conference or other agreed means, as required, to provide comments and respond to questions concerning the matters described in paragraph (a) above. Any in-person participation in Board meetings will be agreed in advance between the Secretariat and the Consultant;
(f) Support the development of relevant guidance for the accreditation process under the RAF, as it relates to the Fund’s fiduciary standards, by providing recommendations and/or written outputs; and
(g) Perform other tasks relevant to the review of accreditation applications in the fiduciary field, as defined by the Secretariat in consultation with the AP.
Required experience and qualifications
1. Master’s degree in finance, accounting, economics, business administration, public administration, law, or another relevant discipline;

2. At least 15 years of relevant experience with an international financial institution, such as a multilateral development bank or major bilateral development agency, in relation to fiduciary standards or comparable institutional requirements, including exposure to public and private sector institutions;

3. Proven experience in conducting institutional fiduciary assessments and due diligence against international standards, including assessment of policies, procedures, internal control arrangements and evidence of implementation;

4. Strong technical expertise in relevant fiduciary areas, including corporate governance and internal control, financial management, procurement, transparency, accountability and integrity arrangements , and institutional project management systems;

5. Demonstrated ability to determine materiality, apply proportional judgement and develop clear, defensible recommendations where evidence is mixed or institutional practice differs from expected international practice;
6. Experience undertaking institutional assessments in developing-country contexts and balancing local capacity constraints with the need to maintain adequate fiduciary safeguards and accountability;
7. Proven ability to work constructively with multiple stakeholders holding different views while preserving the quality, credibility and independence of the assessment;
8. Exceptional interpersonal skills, multicultural awareness, rigor, sound judgement, availability, and a positive and proactive work attitude;
9. Ability to work independently as a self-starter and collaboratively as part of a closely coordinated team to deliver the programme of work;
10. Fluency in written and spoken English. Knowledge of another official United Nations language would be an advantage; and
11. Strong competence and autonomy in the use of standard software programmes, including Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook and web-based platforms.

12. Personal devices used for the assignment must be capable of supporting GCF's current access and security requirements throughout the engagement and, at a minimum, must run: (i) for mobile devices, Android 14 or later or iOS 17 or later; and (ii) for computers, Windows 11 or macOS Ventura or later.
Contract Period and Duty Station: maximum 120 working days for 12 months/ remote
Note: Due to the high volume of applications, only candidates shortlisted for interview will be contacted regarding the status of their application.

Applications from women and nationals of developing countries are strongly encouraged. Candidates of all nationalities are welcome to apply; Closing date for applications is 7 December 2026, 23:59 (KST). Applications received after the closing date may not be considered.
